content: {"id": "a96adb95-907b-419c-b159-abefeb562c75", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "How do I resize an Amazon EBS gp3 volume's IOPS with the AWS CLI?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "629f5d7a-0a64-4cfc-a78e-93a6e92a1fdb", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Resize Amazon EBS gp3 volume IOPS AWS CLI"}]}

{"id": "3989b2c8-9719-4f96-9bf3-371335615a9a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You can modify a gp3 volume's IOPS (and throughput) using the `modify-volume` operation. Here's the command:

```bash
aws ec2 modify-volume \
    --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
    --iops 4000
```

A few things to know:

- **gp3 defaults**: baseline is 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s throughput, included in the storage price. You can provision up to **16,000 IOPS** and **1,000 MiB/s** throughput independently, at extra cost.
- You can combine IOPS and throughput changes in one call:
  ```bash
  aws ec2 modify-volume \
      --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
      --iops 4000 \
      --throughput 250
  ```
- The volume stays attached and in use during the modification — no downtime needed.
- Check progress with:
  ```bash
  aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
  ```
  Look for `ModificationState` to go from `modifying` to `optimizing` to `completed`.
- There's a cooldown: after a modification, you generally need to wait at least 6 hours before the next one on the same volume (unless reverting to a previous config within that window, in some cases).

Want me to check the current IOPS/throughput settings on one of your actual volumes, or look at CloudWatch metrics to help decide what value to set?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
